blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Building general game agents requires both high-level task reasoning and low-latency action control in rapidly changing visual environments. These capabilities favor models with substantially different computational profiles, making them difficult to realize within a single model. In this work, we present TaskFrame, a hierarchical planner-controller framework that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language task planner decomposes a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of atomic instructions and is optimized through supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. The hidden states of special goal tokens that terminate each atomic instruction provide continuous goal embeddings that are cached and reused across control steps. A causal Transformer controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every game step. We train the system in three stages: planner training, controller pretraining, and joint alignment. Experiments in Minecraft show that TaskFrame is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and that in closed-loop evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.
blocks.zh: 在快速变化的视觉环境中,建设一般游戏代理既需要高级任务推理,也需要低纬度动作控制. 这些能力有利于计算剖面图有很大相去甚远的模型,使它们难以在一个单一模型内实现. 在这项工作中,我们提出了TaskFrame,一个分级的规划者控制器框架,将任务级别的规划与帧级键盘和-mouse控制相接. 一个视觉语言的任务规划者将一个高层次的目标分解成一个有序的原子指令序列,并通过监督学习和依赖意识的GPRO来优化. 终止每个原子指令的特殊目标符号的隐藏状态提供连续目标嵌入,被缓存并跨控制步骤再利用. 一个因果变形器控制器将活性目标的嵌入与最近的观测结合起来,以预测离散键盘和鼠标-按钮动作以及每个游戏步骤的持续相机运动. 我们分三个阶段对系统进行培训:规划员培训、控制员预训和联合调整。 在Minecraft的实验显示,TaskFrame在指令分解上与通用视觉语言模型具有竞争力,在闭路评估中,剂的战斗成功率高于被评估的基线.

blocks.en:
Games have long been a demanding testbed for artificial general intelligence
(AGI), as successful gameplay requires the integration of perception, reasoning,
planning, and decision making into goal-directed behavior.
Existing efforts have reached or surpassed expert human
performance in board games, Atari, multiplayer poker, and complex real-time
strategy games ( Silver et al., 2016 ; Silver et al., 2017 ; Schrittwieser et al., 2020 ; OpenAI et al., 2019 ; Badia et al., 2020 ; Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ; Vinyals et al., 2019 ) . More recently, research has shifted
toward embodied game agents that follow language instructions and act
directly from pixels in open-ended virtual worlds ( SIMA Team, 2025 ; Magne et al., 2026 ; Yue et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Hafner et al., 2025 ) . Unlike agents specialized for a fixed environment or
objective, such systems provide a natural setting for studying whether an agent
can understand diverse goals, adapt its behavior to changing visual situations,
and execute complex tasks through a general action interface.

blocks.en:
Building such an embodied agent remains difficult because task-level reasoning
and frame-level control operate at different frequencies. Understanding a scene, grounding an
instruction, and determining the correct sequence of subgoals require a
large, high-capacity model. In contrast, executing those subgoals requires a
lightweight controller that can continuously incorporate the latest frame and
emit actions with low latency. This challenge is especially evident in visually
dynamic games, where abrupt camera motion and sudden events must be handled
through a hybrid action space combining discrete keyboard
presses with continuous mouse movement. Running a large reasoning model at every
control step is prohibitively expensive, whereas a small reactive policy alone
lacks the semantic capacity to reliably interpret and organize complex
instructions and visual history.

Existing work addresses parts of this tension through several strategies. Hierarchical agents use a language model to select skills or produce
high-level plans for a goal-conditioned controller ( Ahn et al., 2022 ; Wang et al., 2023c ; Yuan et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2025b ) . In physical robotics, dual-system Vision-Language-Action (VLA)
models separate a slower semantic module from a faster visuomotor policy ( NVIDIA et al., 2025 ; Figure AI, 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ; Bu et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2025 ) , while action chunking amortizes inference by predicting multiple
actions at once, with recent methods improving parallel decoding or asynchronous
execution ( Kim et al., 2025 ; Black et al., 2025 ) . A practical game agent must
connect these mechanisms through an interface that supports both structured
planning and responsive control. The high-level model must translate an
open-vocabulary goal into a complete and correctly ordered sequence of atomic
goals, and the controller must keep incorporating the latest visual observation
at every action step.

blocks.en:
We present TaskFrame , a hierarchical game agent that connects
task-level planning with frame-level control through planner-produced goal
representations ( Figure 1 ). Its high-capacity task planner is
trained to perform visually grounded instruction decomposition, with dedicated
data and a dependency-aware reinforcement learning objective that addresses both
step-count and ordering correctness. Each atomic goal it emits is terminated by a
special goal token, and the hidden states at these tokens are cached and passed
to a lightweight frame controller as continuous goal embeddings. The
controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent frames to emit
discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every
game step, so the large planner stays outside the frame-level control loop. We
train the system in three stages: the planner is trained for decomposition, the
controller is trained to produce actions from each frame, and the two modules are
finally aligned jointly.

blocks.en:
We train the controller on human gameplay with native keyboard-and-mouse actions
recorded directly from players, and the planner on the hierarchical annotations
of GameHorizon Suite ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , which provide atomic
instructions, compositional goals, and dependency relations.
Our 9B planner outperforms GPT-4o and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on instruction
decomposition. In closed-loop Minecraft evaluation, TaskFrame reaches a 51%
average success rate on combat tasks, the highest among the evaluated models,
and ablations examine each component.
To summarize, our contributions are as follows: • We introduce TaskFrame, a hierarchical game agent in which a
vision-language planner decomposes goals once per task and conditions a
frame-level keyboard-and-mouse controller, which acts at every game step,
through the hidden states of special goal tokens. • We propose a dependency-aware GRPO objective for instruction
decomposition that rewards necessary precedence relations separately from
conventional ordering, derived from pairwise dependency annotations. • We propose a three-stage training recipe that pretrains the controller
with a generic goal encoder and then aligns it with the planner through LoRA
adapters, and we equip the controller with a hybrid discrete and
flow-matching action head. We evaluate the planner on two decomposition
benchmarks and the full agent in closed-loop Minecraft control.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
MineRL and VPT established large-scale imitation from human Minecraft
play ( Guss et al., 2019 ; Baker et al., 2022 ) , and MineDojo added an open-ended environment with
internet-scale knowledge ( Fan et al., 2022 ) . STEVE-1, GROOT, ROCKET-1, and
MineDreamer condition low-level policies on text, reference videos,
visual-temporal prompts, or imagined goals ( Lifshitz et al., 2023 ; Cai et al., 2024b ; Cai et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) ,
while JARVIS-VLA and OmniJARVIS post-train VLMs to emit keyboard-and-mouse actions
directly ( Li et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2024 ) , following robotic
VLAs ( Brohan et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2024 ) . Recent systems generalize across tasks and
games ( Wang et al., 2025 ; SIMA Team, 2025 ; Tan et al., 2025 ; Tan et al., 2024 ) and control games through native
keyboard-and-mouse interfaces at frame rate ( Yue et al., 2026 ; Magne et al., 2026 ) . TaskFrame
instead connects explicit, trained task decomposition to frame-level control and
keeps the large VLM outside the per-frame loop.

blocks.en:
Language-model planners ground decisions in skill affordances ( Ahn et al., 2022 ) ,
use environment feedback ( Huang et al., 2022 ) , or write code over control
primitives ( Liang et al., 2023 ) . In Minecraft, Plan4MC, DEPS, Voyager, JARVIS-1,
and Optimus-1/2 plan over learned skills or dispatch multimodal plans to
goal-conditioned controllers ( Yuan et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023b ; Wang et al., 2023a ; Wang et al., 2023c ; Li et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025b ) . These planners are prompted or supervised to produce plans
but are not optimized for whether their steps respect task dependencies.
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, popularized by GRPO and its
variants ( Shao et al., 2024 ; DeepSeek-AI, 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025 ) , offers a way to do so: we use the
must-precede annotations of GameHorizon Suite ( Wang et al., 2026 ) to define
a reward that separates necessary precedence from conventional ordering.

keyboard-and-mouse actions from visual observations. We build on the

decoded into keyboard and mouse actions. We make two changes: the controller is
conditioned on the planner’s vision-language goal embedding in addition to the
visual observation, and continuous camera motion is modeled with a flow-matching
head for smooth control.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented TaskFrame, a hierarchical game agent that separates task-level
planning from frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language planner, trained with supervised
decomposition and dependency-aware GRPO, turns a high-level instruction into an
ordered sequence of atomic goals and outperforms
general-purpose models such as GPT-4o and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on instruction
decomposition. The hidden states of the goal tokens in its plan serve as goal
embeddings. A causal Transformer controller with a hybrid action head converts the active embedding and
recent frames into native actions at every game step. In closed-loop Minecraft
evaluation, the agent achieves the highest combat success rate among all evaluated
models. Ablations further show that the controller relies on the goal condition and
that the aligned goal embeddings are more effective than passing decoded text
between the two modules.

最近,每个游戏步骤都将它设定为本地动作。 在密闭式地雷中

The agent does not decide on its own when an atomic goal is done, so it relies
on an external execution protocol to switch to the next goal, and it does not
replan after a failure. In addition, the controller sees only about one second
of history, which is short for long-horizon tasks.
Finally, all experiments are conducted in Minecraft, and extending the method to
other games remains a challenging direction for future work.

blocks.en: A.6 Why naive SFT generalizes poorly
blocks.zh: A.6 联合国 为什么SFT天真地概括不好

blocks.en:
Our first SFT run balanced categories by duplicating minority examples. Its
training loss decreased steadily, but on an external diagnostic built from
VPT-20h (539 four-way questions over 498 clips that share no recordings with our
training data; chance is 25%), accuracy fell to 39.5%, below the backbone’s
51.2%. Grouping questions by how closely the gold steps match the phrasing of
the training annotations shows that the SFT model beats the backbone on the most
familiar quartile (76.1% vs. 70.1%) but falls below chance on the least
familiar one (17.0% vs. 35.6%). The model thus learns a narrow decomposition
skill tied to annotation phrasing, which a clip-level holdout from the training
distribution did not expose. These findings motivated our SFT recipe
( Section A.1 ): we balance categories by downsampling thematic
examples instead of duplicating minority ones, describe each atomic target in two
styles, and paraphrase high-level instructions.
